comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C4, C44, C49-C54. Both evaluate ABHD2 knockdown and rescue experiments as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes experimental controls and quantification; peer reviewers initially raised concerns about construct specificity and sample sizes but were satisfied after revision.

Strong agreement on claims C55-C62 regarding lipase domain requirement. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights systematic mutagenesis and structure-function rigor; peer reviewers recognized this as a key finding demonstrating that acyltransferase activity is dispensable.

Significant disagreement on lipidomics data (C64-C69, C45). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with praise for comprehensive analysis; peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN citing presentation issues (heat maps inadequate), incomplete interpretation, and inconsistencies between figures that persisted after revision.

Disagreement on prostaglandin measurements (C70-C73). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN due to technical problems: PGE2/D2 require separate measurements, PGI2 half-life issues necessitate measuring 6-keto-PGF1α instead, concerns not adequately addressed in revision.

Both address S1P measurements (C74) but with different emphasis. OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, noting the negative result and secretion explanation; peer reviewers (UNCERTAIN) emphasize the critical inconsistency between demonstrated S1PR3 functional role (C104-C111) and lack of detectable S1P changes, undermining mechanistic interpretation.

Significant disagreement on pharmacological studies (C75-C93). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, praising dose-response curves and controls; peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN citing high inhibitor concentrations causing potential non-specific effects, insufficient target engagement data, and selectivity concerns persisting after revision.

Partial overlap on autotaxin inhibitor studies (C84-C86). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers raised broader concerns about pharmacological specificity across multiple inhibitors including HA130, evaluating the entire pharmacology set as UNCERTAIN.

Partial overlap on Cox inhibitor studies (C87-C91). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with praise for isoform specificity; peer reviewers grouped this with other pharmacology and evaluated as UNCERTAIN due to general concerns about inhibitor concentrations and specificity.
Partial overlap on lipoxygenase inhibitor effects (C92-C93). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers included this in broader pharmacology concerns evaluated as UNCERTAIN.

Strong agreement on ceramidase mutant analysis (C94-C98). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this rules out ceramidase activity as essential; peer reviewers acknowledged this as an important negative result clarifying which enzymatic activities are not required.

Partial overlap on ceramidase inhibition (C99-C103). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED noting weaker effects suggest redundancy; peer reviewers grouped with S1P/S1PR3 findings and evaluated as UNCERTAIN due to inconsistency between S1PR3 functional role and lack of S1P changes.

Agreement on S1PR3 knockdown experiments (C104-C111). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, highlighting the dissociation between signaling pathways; peer reviewers noted the functional demonstration but evaluated as UNCERTAIN due to the critical inconsistency with lack of detectable S1P changes.

Agreement on G-protein inhibitor studies (C112-C115) but different confidence levels. OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, noting 'puzzling findings' and unclear selectivity/interpretation despite accepting general G-protein involvement.

Agreement on in vitro PLA2 assays (C116-C120) but different initial confidence. OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, calling this a key mechanistic finding; peer reviewers initially found results 'intriguing and puzzling,' questioning whether the system works as claimed, but were satisfied after revision (implicit SUPPORTED).
Both address tobacco lysate PLA2 assays (C121-C122). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers' initial concerns about the in vitro system applied here as well, though satisfied after revision.

Perfect agreement on co-immunoprecipitation experiments (C123-C127). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes P4-enhanced interaction and independence from enzymatic activity; peer reviewers acknowledged this supports the co-receptor model without specific concerns.

Strong agreement on endocytosis imaging (C128-C131). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the requirement for ABHD2 and PLA2 activity; peer reviewers recognized this as an important mechanistic link between enzymatic activity and receptor trafficking.

Strong agreement on SNAP25Δ20 experiments (C132-C138). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval praises the sophisticated design separating endocytosis from signaling; peer reviewers accepted this as demonstrating ABHD2 functions at multiple steps beyond triggering endocytosis.

Both address pharmacology with SNAP25Δ20 (C139-C141). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers grouped with SNAP25 experiments and evaluated as SUPPORTED, though their broader pharmacology concerns (R6) may apply.

Both address the central co-receptor discovery (C5, C46, C152). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with multiple lines of evidence; peer reviewers initially questioned the in vitro reconstitution but were satisfied after revision, implicitly supporting the overall finding.
Partial overlap on bifurcation model (C6-C7, C47). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers acknowledged the endocytosis-signaling link as SUPPORTED, consistent with the bifurcation concept.

Both address overall conclusions and model (C6-C7, C47, C150, C156, C158). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED, endorsing overall conclusions and significance despite some unresolved mechanistic details.

Both address main conclusion of obligate co-receptor model (C8). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with comprehensive evidence; peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED, recognizing novelty and broad significance despite some technical concerns with specific experiments.

Both address speculation about MAGL activity regulation (C153-C155). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN noting lack of direct testing; peer reviewers evaluate overall conclusions as SUPPORTED but did not specifically address this speculative point.

Both address speculation about lysophospholipids and membrane curvature (C157). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN, noting this is plausible but unproven; peer reviewers did not specifically address this hypothesis in their overall SUPPORTED evaluation of conclusions.

Both address extrapolation beyond Xenopus system (C151, C160). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation; peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED, emphasizing broad physiological implications while acknowledging findings are from oocytes.

Peer reviewers evaluated background/literature claims (C1-C3, C9-C43) as SUPPORTED, acknowledging established context. OpenEval did not produce a separate result for these background claims, which provide necessary context but are not novel findings.
